terms.gloss: mop; a swab of tails, or a long sponge, for wiping
evidence: Ter. Eun. 4.7.7, as cited by Lewis & Short
terms.comment: The Romans’ wiper, made of an ox-tail or a long sponge: pēniculī spongiae longae propter similitūdinem caudārum appellātae (Paul. ex Fest. p. 208 Müll.). The lexicon also uses it for a brush (pastry brush, toothbrush).

phrases.latin: Juventūs nōmen fēcit Pēniculō mihi, ideō quia mēnsam, quandō edō, dētergeō.
phrases.english: The young men named me Peniculus, ‘Swab’, because when I eat I wipe the table clean.

sources: Plautus and Festus as Lewis & Short quotes them. Traupman, Morgan–Owens and Levi–Bini have no word for a mop.
